title: Alteration of the fecal microbiota in Chinese patients with Parkinson's disease.
quotes: Genera Clostridium IV, Aquabacterium, Holdemania, Sphingomonas, Clostridium XVIII, Butyricicoccus and Anaerotruncus were enriched in the feces of PD patients after adjusting for age, gender, body mass index (BMI), and constipation.
note: Butyricicoccus explicitly reported as enriched in PD patients vs. presumed healthy controls.

title: Compositional and functional gut microbiota alterations in mild cognitive impairment: links to Alzheimer's disease pathology.
quotes: Notably, species within the same genera, such as Bacteroides and Ruminococcus , showed opposing effects, while Akkermansia muciniphila correlated with reduced amyloid burden, suggesting a protective role.
Similarly, Akkermansia muciniphila , a well-known next-generation probiotic, showed a negative correlation with amyloid positivity.
note: Sentences describe correlations within MCI/AD patients or interventions, not comparisons to healthy controls.

title: Differential Patterns of Gut and Oral Microbiomes in Hispanic Individuals with Cognitive Impairment.
quotes: Conversely, CI individuals exhibited a decreased abundance of gut genera, including Shuttleworthia , Holdemania , and Subdoligranulum , which are known for their anti-inflammatory properties.
Specifically, individuals with CI exhibited an increased abundance of Bacteroides and Escherichia-Shigella , and a decreased abundance of Ruminococcus and Subdoligranulum .
note: CI (diseased) individuals explicitly compared to controls; Subdoligranulum decreased in CI.

title: Gut microbiome alterations in preclinical Alzheimer's disease
quotes: The GLM analysis revealed that the genera Megamonas, Serratia, Leptotrichia and Clostridium (family Clostridiaceae) were increased in the Aβ+ CN group compared to the Aβ− CN group, whereas the genera CF231, Victivallis, Enterococcus, Mitsuokella and Clostridium (family Erysipelotrichaceae) were decreased in Aβ+ CN (Table 2 and Fig 1) In the ROC analysis, the logistic regression model with variables representing the presence or absence of each of the nine genera effectively distinguish Aβ+ and Aβ− CN with the AUC value of 0.
note: Comparison is between two subgroups of cognitively-normal individuals (Aβ+ vs Aβ-), not diseased vs. healthy.

title: Gut- and oral-dysbiosis differentially impact spinal- and bulbar-onset ALS, predicting ALS severity and potentially determining the location of disease onset.

title: Identification of disordered profiles of gut microbiota and functional component in stroke and poststroke epilepsy
quotes: At the genus level, the relative abundance of butyricicoccus was the most markedly decreased in STR compared with CON (Figure 3a ).

title: Transmission of Alzheimer's disease-associated microbiota dysbiosis and its impact on cognitive function: evidence from mice and patients.
quotes: Notably, AD Tg mice (statistical significance) and ADWT mice (trending) also exhibited increased abundance of Ruminiclostridium-5 ( Fig. 3s ), the bacteria associated with mucosa-related microbiome and obesity [ 58 ], and decreased abundance of Lachnoclostridium ( Fig. 3t ), a novel marker for colorectal cancer [ 59 ], compared to those in WT mice.
note: AD transgenic mice (diseased) compared to WT mice (healthy); Lachnoclostridium decreased in AD.
